newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile gov't backs Central Bank rates cut - minister.
newsitem.headline: Chile gov't backs Central Bank rates cut - minister.

text.p: The Chilean government supported the Central Bank's decision Thursday to relax its tight monetary policy and trim domestic interest rates, said acting Finance Minister Manuel Marfan Friday.
"We support the decision of the Central Bank's council to moderate its monetary policy as a result of progress seen in macro-economic indicators," Marfan told reporters.
"The modification is very gradual but opportune, even through after the measures interest rates are still those of (a period) of adjustment."
The bank clipped daily interbank rates by 0.25 percentage point to 7.25 percent, in a move which caught Chilean financial markets by surprise.
Blue chip shares soared over two percent Friday with investors jubilant at the first easing of the bank's year-long tight credit policy which has put a lid on stock prices.
The policy, heavily criticized by industry in recent months, has succeeded in its aim of taming Chile's strong economic growth, said Marfan.
"It is a light, prudent reduction, but it reflects greater tranquility seen in the current economic situation," he said.
The bank first jacked up rates in October 1995 and then again more severely in April 1996 as the authorities feared the robust growth was threatening to ignite inflation.
The latest economic indicators show that Chile's economy will meet the official inflation target for the year of 5.5 percent, said Marfan.
Consumer prices rose 6.6 percent last year, slightly above the goverment's target of 6.5 percent.
